title: The v1 Renaissance synthesis is unsourced
summary: Dates, the hero list, and the claim that the Renaissance founded modernity were not tied to a source.
body: The v1 article dates the Renaissance from about 1350 to 1600, starts it in Florence, Venice, and Rome, and lists humanism, Leonardo, Michelangelo, Raphael, Copernicus, and Galileo as a single movement that founded modern science and secular education. That is a nineteenth-century style of periodization. It can be useful and it can hide merchants, women, plague, and non-Italian work. No Burckhardt page or museum essay was successfully read. Leave the synthesis unsourced. Gutenberg's Bible and the later scientific texts are sourced on their own cards.
